Atom SDK — C# Version

Introduction

The Atom SDK C# version is the official client library for .NET developers. It is designed based on the async/await pattern and provides strongly typed encapsulation of all REST interfaces of the Atom platform. All network calls are non-blocking asynchronous methods, naturally supporting high concurrency scenarios. Target framework is .NET 6 and above.

SDK Core Features

Features Description

Fully asynchronous API

All Service methods return Task<T>, support async/await

Strongly typed overloading

Each interface provides two sets of return values JsonElement (original) and specific model class

CancellationToken

All methods accept optional CancellationToken for caller-initiated cancellation

Poll timeout

Graph running and node activation interface supports timeout named parameters, default 30 seconds, timeout throws AtomTimeoutException

Unified exception system

AtomApiException / AtomHttpException / AtomProtocolException / AtomTimeoutException

Target framework

The ordinary object result will automatically carry the status field of this request, and the strongly typed result can be read directly result.Status. Lists, booleans, raw byte[], parsed point clouds, bound raw values, and node parameter snapshots maintain the original data shape.

Installation

Prerequisite: .NET 6 SDK or later.

First download atom_sdk_<version>.zip from the Download Center and extract it. The C package is <SDK_DIR>/csharp/AtomSdk.<version>.nupkg; no additional NuGet source configuration is required.

Step 1: Install the package

dotnet add package AtomSdk --version <version> \
  --source <SDK_DIR>/csharp

You can also add it to .csproj:

<PackageReference Include="AtomSdk" Version="<version>" />

If the package cannot be found, confirm that <SDK_DIR>/csharp contains AtomSdk.<version>.nupkg and that --version matches the version in the file name.

namespace

using AtomSdk;                // AtomClient
using AtomSdk.Services;      // GraphService, NodeService, GraphNodeService, RuntimeService
using AtomSdk.Models;        // RuntimeFrame,RuntimePassiveBinoFrame,RuntimePassiveBinoImage and various model classes
using AtomSdk.Core;          // Exception type
using System.Text.Json;      // JsonElement

Big Four Service Responsibilities Overview

Service Access entrance Responsibilities

GraphService

client.Graph

Complete life cycle management of the main image (create, delete, copy, load, run, export, etc.)

NodeService

client.Node

Add, delete, modify, check, disconnect, parameter read and write, and single node operation of nodes in the main graph

GraphNodeService

client.GraphNode Node operations inside the

subgraph node (GraphNode), the interface corresponds to NodeService but has one more layer graphNodeId

RuntimeService

client.Runtime Graph loading, frame inference, parameter setting, and binding value reading in the

Runtime environment

Structured parameter naming

The complex interface maintains the same set of parameter object naming as Python SDK: * *Ref: refers to an existing object and is only responsible for locating resources, such as NodeRef, PortRef, BindingRef * *Params: Complete input parameters of an interface call, such as CreateGraphParams, RuntimeRunParams * *Update: Modify existing configurations or values, such as NodeParamUpdate, RuntimeParamsUpdate

await client.Graph.CreateGraphInfoAsync(new CreateGraphParams("my_graph"));
await client.Node.CreateNodeInfoAsync(new CreateNodeParams("my_graph", "ResizeImage"));
// Normal mode example;passive_bino Please use mode RuntimeRunParams.PassiveBinoFromFile/Bytes/Images.
await client.Runtime.RunGraphAsync(new RuntimeRunParams("my_graph", new[] { frame }));

For more information about the construction method of parameter objects, file uploading and error-prone points, see 参数对象.

quick start

Create client

using AtomSdk;

// baseUrl for Atom Platform service address,For example "http://localhost:8080"
var client = new AtomClient("http://localhost:8080");

Complete async Main example

using System;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using AtomSdk;
using AtomSdk.Core;
using AtomSdk.Models;

class Program
{
    static async Task Main(string[] args)
    {
        var client = new AtomClient("http://localhost:8080");

        try
        {
            // 1. Create a graph
            var graphInfo = await client.Graph.CreateGraphInfoAsync(new CreateGraphParams("my_graph"));
            Console.WriteLine($"Diagram created,ID: {graphInfo.GraphId}, Request status: {graphInfo.Status}");

            // 2. List all pictures
            var graphs = await client.Graph.ListGraphSummariesAsync();
            Console.WriteLine($"Currently there are {graphs.Length} pictures");

            // 3. open diagram(Get timestamp)
            await client.Graph.OpenGraphAsync("my_graph");

            // 4. Create nodes in the graph
            var nodeInfo = await client.Node.CreateNodeInfoAsync(new CreateNodeParams("my_graph", "ResizeImage"));
            Console.WriteLine($"Node has been created,ID: {nodeInfo.NodeId}, Request status: {nodeInfo.Status}");

            // 5. Run chart
            var runResult = await client.Graph.RunGraphResultAsync("my_graph");
            Console.WriteLine($"Run completed,Request status: {runResult.Status}");

            // 6. release chart
            await client.Graph.ReleaseGraphAsync("my_graph");
        }
        catch (AtomApiException ex)
        {
            Console.WriteLine($"Server error {ex.Status}: {ex.Message}");
        }
        catch (AtomHttpException ex)
        {
            Console.WriteLine($"HTTP Error {ex.StatusCode}: {ex.Message}");
        }
    }
}

Called in synchronous code

If the project does not support async/await (such as Unity non-main thread, old framework), you can wait synchronously in the following way:

// Method one:GetAwaiter().GetResult()(Recommended,Keep stack information)
var result = client.Graph.CreateGraphAsync(new CreateGraphParams("my_graph")).GetAwaiter().GetResult();

// Method 2:Task.Run().Result(Suitable for console or testing)
var result = Task.Run(() => client.Graph.CreateGraphAsync(new CreateGraphParams("my_graph"))).Result;
Using .Result or .GetAwaiter().GetResult() within ASP.NET or WinForms/WPF within SynchronizationContext may result in deadlock, it is recommended to always use await.

Unified error handling

try
{
    var result = await client.Graph.CreateGraphAsync(new CreateGraphParams("my_graph"));
}
catch (AtomApiException ex)
{
    // The server returned a business error(Picture already exists,Parameters are illegal etc.)
    Console.WriteLine($"Server error {ex.Status}: {ex.Message}");
    if (ex.Payload.HasValue)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"Error details: {ex.Payload.Value}");
    }
}
catch (AtomTimeoutException ex)
{
    // Graph run or node activation never completed,SDK Poll wait timeout
    Console.WriteLine($"Timeout waiting for interface to complete: {ex.Path}, attempts={ex.Attempts}");
    Console.WriteLine($"last response: {ex.LastData}");
}
catch (AtomHttpException ex)
{
    // HTTP layer error(Such as 404,500,Connection refused etc.)
    Console.WriteLine($"HTTP Error {ex.StatusCode}: {ex.Message}");
}
catch (AtomProtocolException ex)
{
    // Response protocol parsing failed
    Console.WriteLine($"protocol error: {ex.Message}");
}

JsonElement Field Access Quick Reference

The original return value of SDK is System.Text.Json.JsonElement, and the access method is as follows:

var result = await client.Graph.CreateGraphAsync(new CreateGraphParams("my_graph"));

// Read string(add ! Assert not empty)
string id = result.GetProperty("graphId").GetString()!;

// read numbers
double ts = result.GetProperty("timestamp").GetDouble();

// Read integer
int count = result.GetProperty("count").GetInt32();

// Read request status
int status = result.GetProperty("status").GetInt32();

// Traverse array
foreach (var item in result.GetProperty("nodes").EnumerateArray())
{
    string name = item.GetProperty("nodeName").GetString()!;
}

// Determine whether the field exists(optional fields)
if (result.TryGetProperty("description", out var desc))
{
    Console.WriteLine(desc.GetString());
}
